input.strategy_title: GPU chargeback reporting for platform administrators
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Platform teams fund shared GPU clusters but cannot attribute consumption to the
projects using them, so capacity costs are socialized and heavy users have no
incentive to release resources. The in-flight metering strategy
(RHAISTRAT-9990) is delivering per-project GPU-hour usage data; this strategy
builds the administrator-facing chargeback reporting on top of that data. The
metering data schema is owned by RHAISTRAT-9990 and is not final until that
strategy lands — reporting work here consumes it, and must not re-implement
collection.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges, computed from the metering data delivered by RHAISTRAT-9990. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Reports can be exported as CSV and retrieved via a stable API for finance tooling. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | The Dashboard admin view shows current-month consumption against each project's Kueue quota. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers report semantics (what counts as a GPU-hour) and export integration. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- The metering collection pipeline itself (RHAISTRAT-9990)
- Currency/cost-rate modelling — reports are in GPU-hours, not dollars

## Open Questions

1. The metering data schema finalizes only when RHAISTRAT-9990 lands; report
   implementation consuming it carries that external timing risk.

# Per-project GPU-hour consumption reporting backend

## Description

This epic delivers the backend capability that computes per-project GPU-hour
consumption reports over selectable time ranges from the metering data
delivered by the GPU usage metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990), and exposes
those reports through a stable API and CSV export for administrators and
finance tooling. It consumes the metering data; it does not re-implement
metering collection.

## Scope

- Compute per-project GPU-hour consumption reports aggregated over
  administrator-selectable time ranges, sourced from the per-project GPU-hour
  usage data delivered by the GPU usage metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990).
- Expose report retrieval through a stable API suitable for finance tooling
  integration.
- Provide CSV export of the reports.
- Keep the metering-schema consumption isolated in the report computation
  layer so that changes in the (not-yet-final) metering data schema are
  absorbed there without reworking the reporting API or export surfaces.
- No metering collection pipeline work (owned by RHAISTRAT-9990) and no
  currency/cost-rate modelling — reports are denominated in GPU-hours.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-project GPU-hour consumption reports can be computed over
  administrator-selectable time ranges.
- Reports are computed from the metering data delivered by the GPU usage
  metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990); no collection logic is re-implemented
  here.
- Reports are retrievable via a stable API usable by finance tooling.
- Reports are exportable as CSV.
- The consumption layer reflects the finalized metering data schema once the
  GPU usage metering strategy lands — schema drift is absorbed in the
  consumption layer without changing the reporting API contract.
- The existing build and test pipeline for the affected repository remains
  green.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable
  time ranges computed from the metering data delivered by RHAISTRAT-9990
  (computation and retrieval half; the administrator viewing surface is
  delivered by the Dashboard admin view epic).
- **HLR-2 (P1, bundled)** — CSV export and stable API retrieval for finance
  tooling, bundled because it is a presentation/transport mode of the same
  report computation and data structure as HLR-1.

## Risks / Notes

- External timing risk: the metering data schema finalizes only when
  RHAISTRAT-9990 lands. Work can proceed against the current draft schema with
  drift absorbed in the consumption layer, but final validation of the report
  semantics waits on the finalized schema. This timing is externally
  controlled and is tracked here as a risk, not an acceptance criterion on
  schedule.

# Dashboard admin view for GPU chargeback reporting

## Description

This epic delivers the administrator-facing Dashboard view for GPU chargeback
reporting: per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time
ranges, plus a current-month consumption display compared against each
project's Kueue quota. It renders data retrieved from the consumption
reporting backend's stable API and quota information from the platform's
Kueue quota model.

## Scope

- Admin-facing view in the Dashboard console listing per-project GPU-hour
  consumption reports over administrator-selectable time ranges, backed by the
  stable reporting API and report data delivered by the consumption reporting
  backend.
- Current-month per-project consumption displayed against each project's
  Kueue quota (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model).
- Access restricted to platform administrators (admin-role view), consistent
  with existing Dashboard admin surfaces.
- The view is gated by the Dashboard's per-component feature-flag mechanism
  (OdhDashboardConfig), defaulting to disabled until the feature is ready.
- No metering collection, no report computation, and no currency/cost-rate
  modelling — the view renders GPU-hours delivered by the reporting backend.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over
  selectable time ranges in the Dashboard admin view.
- The admin view displays current-month consumption against each project's
  Kueue quota.
- Report data shown in the view is retrieved from the stable reporting API
  (no parallel consumption computation in the Dashboard).
- The view is behind a Dashboard feature flag (OdhDashboardConfig) and is
  disabled by default.
- The existing Dashboard build and test pipeline remains green.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — the administrator viewing surface for per-project GPU-hour
  consumption reports over selectable time ranges (the computation and API
  half is delivered by the consumption reporting backend epic).
- **HLR-3 (P1, bundled)** — current-month consumption against each project's
  Kueue quota, bundled because it renders in the same Dashboard admin view
  surface as the HLR-1 time-range reports; a split would build the same UI
  surface twice.

## Risks / Notes

- The view depends on the reporting API contract from the consumption
  reporting backend; work on view scaffolding, quota display, and feature
  flagging can proceed in parallel, but final wiring waits on the stable API.

# GPU chargeback reporting documentation

## Description

This epic delivers the documentation for GPU chargeback reporting: report
semantics (what counts as a GPU-hour) and export/API integration guidance for
finance tooling, plus coverage of the Dashboard admin view. It is authored
through the Red Hat docs content process after the implementation epics land,
so the content describes what was actually built.

## Scope

- Document report semantics: what counts as a GPU-hour, how per-project
  attribution works, and what time ranges cover.
- Document export integration: how finance tooling retrieves reports via the
  stable API and CSV export.
- Document the Dashboard admin view, including the current-month
  consumption-versus-Kueue-quota comparison.
- Technical review of all content against the delivered reporting backend and
  Dashboard admin view before publication.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation defines report semantics, including what counts as
  a GPU-hour and how per-project attribution is computed.
- Published documentation covers export integration (stable API and CSV) for
  finance tooling.
- Published documentation covers the Dashboard admin view and the
  consumption-versus-quota comparison.
- All content is technically reviewed against the implemented reporting
  backend and Dashboard admin view.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)** — documentation covering report semantics (what counts as a
  GPU-hour) and export integration.

## Notes

- Epic priority is P1 per the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy
  priority Major → P1), not inherited from the implementation epics.
- Documentation waits for both implementation epics because it describes the
  delivered report semantics, API/export surface, and admin view.

The externally-controlled schema timing is correctly kept in Risks/Notes rather than filed as a schedule AC — the right treatment.
